name: Learn: Deployments & Jobs
objective: CKAD › Application Deployment (20%). Goal: create and scale Deployments, roll out a new image and confirm it, roll back to the previous version, and run batch work with Jobs and CronJobs — the workload-lifecycle tasks the exam leans on.
description: Learn the core CKAD workload objects step by step — create and scale a Deployment, perform a rolling update and confirm the rollout advanced, roll it back, then drive batch work with a Job (completions + parallelism) and a scheduled CronJob with a concurrencyPolicy.

questions.title: Create and scale a Deployment
questions.teach:
A **Deployment** manages a replicated, self-healing set of Pods through a ReplicaSet. You declare a desired *image*, a *replica count*, and the *pod labels* its selector matches; the controller keeps reality matching that spec.

**Ways to create / scale:**
- `kubectl create deployment NAME --image=IMG --replicas=N` — fast imperative path.
- `kubectl create deployment NAME --image=IMG --dry-run=client -o yaml` — scaffold YAML you then edit and `apply`.
- `kubectl scale deployment NAME --replicas=M` — change the desired count. You can also `kubectl edit`, patch `.spec.replicas`, or re-`apply` an edited manifest.
- `kubectl autoscale deployment NAME --min=2 --max=5 --cpu-percent=80` creates an HPA (which then owns `replicas`).

**Gotchas:**
- The selector and pod-template labels default to `app=NAME`. `.spec.selector` is **immutable** after creation — you can't repoint it later.
- The container is named after the deployment (`NAME`); remember this for later `set image` commands.
- If an **HPA** manages the Deployment, a manual `scale` is transient — the HPA will override it.
- `kubectl scale --current-replicas=X --replicas=M` only scales if the current count matches X (safe conditional scale).
questions.prompt:
In namespace `workloads-learn`, create a Deployment named `web` using image `nginx:1.25` with `2` replicas, then scale it to `4` replicas.

Target: Deployment `web` has `4` ready replicas, pod template image `nginx:1.25`, and selector label `app=web`.
questions.hint: `kubectl -n workloads-learn create deployment web --image=nginx:1.25 --replicas=2`, then `kubectl -n workloads-learn scale deployment web --replicas=4`. Check with `kubectl -n workloads-learn get deploy web`.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n workloads-learn create deployment web --image=nginx:1.25 --replicas=2
kubectl -n workloads-learn scale deployment web --replicas=4
kubectl -n workloads-learn get deployment web -o wide   # 4/4 ready, image nginx:1.25

verification.description: Deployment web exists with image nginx:1.25 and selector app=web
Deployment web is scaled to 4 ready replicas

questions.title: Rolling update: set a new image
questions.teach:
A **rolling update** replaces Pods gradually so the app stays available. Changing the pod template (e.g. the container image) bumps the Deployment's **generation** and triggers a new ReplicaSet rollout.

**Ways to change the image / trigger a rollout:**
- `kubectl set image deployment/NAME CONTAINER=NEWIMG` — targeted image swap.
- `kubectl edit deployment NAME` or `kubectl patch` the pod template, or re-`apply` an edited manifest.
- `kubectl rollout restart deployment/NAME` — re-roll with no spec change (handy to pick up a changed ConfigMap/Secret).
- Confirm with `kubectl rollout status deployment/NAME`; `kubectl rollout pause/resume` lets you batch multiple edits into one rollout.

**Strategy (`.spec.strategy`):**
- `RollingUpdate` (default) tuned by `maxSurge` (extra pods allowed) and `maxUnavailable` (pods that can be down) — both accept a number or percent.
- `Recreate` kills all old pods before creating new ones (brief downtime, but no two versions coexist).

**Gotchas:**
- The container name must match exactly in `set image`. With `kubectl create deployment web --image=nginx:1.25` the container is named after the **image** (`nginx`), **not** the deployment — check with `kubectl get deploy web -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].name}'` before `set image`.
- A rollout only happens if the **pod template** actually changes; editing something outside `.spec.template` won't roll.
- `--record` is **deprecated** — set a `kubernetes.io/change-cause` annotation instead to label revisions in history.
- `revisionHistoryLimit` (default 10) caps how many old ReplicaSets are kept for rollback.
questions.prompt:
Perform a rolling update of Deployment `web` to image `nginx:1.26`, and wait for the rollout to finish.

Target: the update to `nginx:1.26` creates a new revision (`.metadata.generation` ≥ 2) and its ReplicaSet is recorded in the Deployment's history — this evidence persists even after you roll back in step 3.
questions.hint: The container is named `web` (matches the deployment). Run `kubectl -n workloads-learn set image deployment/web web=nginx:1.26`, then `kubectl -n workloads-learn rollout status deployment/web`.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n workloads-learn set image deployment/web nginx=nginx:1.26
kubectl -n workloads-learn rollout status deployment/web
kubectl -n workloads-learn get deployment web -o wide   # image nginx:1.26

verification.description: a rollout to nginx:1.26 is recorded in web's ReplicaSet history

questions.title: Rollback to the previous version
questions.teach:
Every rollout is recorded in the Deployment's **revision history** (one ReplicaSet per revision). `kubectl rollout undo deployment/NAME` reverts the pod template to the previous revision — the standard fix when a new image misbehaves.

**Inspecting and targeting revisions:**
- `kubectl rollout history deployment/NAME` lists revisions; add `--revision=N` to see one revision's pod template.
- `kubectl rollout undo deployment/NAME --to-revision=N` rolls back to a **specific** revision (`--to-revision=0`, the default, means the previous one).
- The `kubernetes.io/change-cause` annotation is what shows in the CHANGE-CAUSE column, so set it on each meaningful change.

**Gotchas:**
- An undo is itself a **new** rollout — it creates a new revision; it does not delete the bad one from history.
- You can only roll back to revisions still kept by `revisionHistoryLimit` (default 10). If old ReplicaSets were pruned, that revision is gone.
- Rollback restores the **whole pod template** of that revision (image, env, resources, etc.), not just the image.
- After an undo always re-check `kubectl rollout status` — the revert still rolls gradually per the strategy.
questions.prompt:
The `nginx:1.26` image is causing trouble. Roll back Deployment `web` so its image returns to `nginx:1.25`.

Target: after the undo, Deployment `web` pod template image is `nginx:1.25` again and the rollout is complete.
questions.hint: `kubectl -n workloads-learn rollout undo deployment/web`, then `kubectl -n workloads-learn rollout status deployment/web`. Verify the image with `kubectl -n workloads-learn get deploy web -o wide`.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n workloads-learn rollout undo deployment/web
kubectl -n workloads-learn rollout status deployment/web
kubectl -n workloads-learn get deployment web -o wide   # back to nginx:1.25

verification.description: web pod template image reverted to nginx:1.25

questions.title: Job with completions and parallelism
questions.teach:
A **Job** runs Pods to successful completion — batch work, not long-lived services. `.spec.completions` is how many successful Pods are required; `.spec.parallelism` is how many run at once. With `completions: 6` and `parallelism: 2`, the Job runs Pods two at a time until six have succeeded.

**Key fields:**
- `completions` + `parallelism` — total successes required / concurrency. Leave both unset (or just set `parallelism`) for a single-run or work-queue style Job.
- `backoffLimit` — retries before the Job is marked failed (default 6).
- `activeDeadlineSeconds` — hard wall-clock cap; the Job fails when exceeded.
- `completionMode: Indexed` — each pod gets a fixed index (`JOB_COMPLETION_INDEX`), for partitioned work; default is `NonIndexed`.
- `ttlSecondsAfterFinished` — auto-delete the Job (and its pods) this long after it finishes.

**Gotchas:**
- `restartPolicy` **must** be `Never` or `OnFailure` — `Always` is rejected for Jobs (and CronJobs).
- There's no imperative flag for `completions`/`parallelism`, so scaffold with `kubectl create job NAME --image=IMG --dry-run=client -o yaml` and edit, or write YAML directly (`apiVersion: batch/v1`).
- With `OnFailure` a failing container is restarted in place; with `Never` a new pod is created each failure (watch pod sprawl against `backoffLimit`).
- A completed Job is **not** deleted automatically unless you set `ttlSecondsAfterFinished`.
questions.prompt:
In `workloads-learn`, create a Job named `pi` that must reach `6` successful completions running `2` at a time, using image `busybox:1.36` with command `sh -c 'exit 0'`.

Target: Job `pi` has `.spec.completions=6` and `.spec.parallelism=2`, and reaches 6 successes.
questions.hint: Write YAML with `spec.completions: 6`, `spec.parallelism: 2`, restartPolicy `Never`, container image `busybox:1.36`, command `["sh","-c","exit 0"]`. Apply it, then `kubectl -n workloads-learn get job pi`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: pi
  namespace: workloads-learn
spec:
  completions: 6
  parallelism: 2
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      containers:
      - name: pi
        image: busybox:1.36
        command: ["sh","-c","exit 0"]
EOF
kubectl -n workloads-learn get job pi

verification.description: Job pi has completions=6 and parallelism=2

questions.title: CronJob with schedule and concurrencyPolicy
questions.teach:
A **CronJob** creates Jobs on a schedule (standard 5-field cron syntax). Schedule `*/5 * * * *` means every 5 minutes. The CronJob owns a `jobTemplate`, which in turn owns a pod template.

**Key fields:**
- `concurrencyPolicy` — overlap handling: `Allow` (default), `Forbid` (skip a new run while the previous is still going), or `Replace` (kill the running one and start fresh).
- `startingDeadlineSeconds` — if a scheduled run is missed by more than this, skip it rather than fire late.
- `suspend: true` — pause scheduling without deleting the CronJob.
- `successfulJobsHistoryLimit` / `failedJobsHistoryLimit` — how many finished Jobs to retain (defaults 3 / 1).

**Gotchas:**
- The nested pod template still needs `restartPolicy: Never` or `OnFailure` — same rule as Jobs.
- `concurrencyPolicy` is a field on the **CronJob** spec, not the jobTemplate — `kubectl create cronjob` has no flag for it, so edit/patch or write YAML (`apiVersion: batch/v1`).
- `Forbid` only prevents overlap; it does not catch up on missed runs.
- Schedules run in the kube-controller-manager's timezone unless you set `.spec.timeZone` (e.g. `"Etc/UTC"`).
- Quote the schedule string in YAML (`"*/5 * * * *"`) so the `*` isn't mis-parsed.
questions.prompt:
In `workloads-learn`, create a CronJob named `report` with schedule `*/5 * * * *` and `concurrencyPolicy: Forbid`, whose Job runs image `busybox:1.36` with command `sh -c 'date'`.

Target: CronJob `report` has `.spec.schedule='*/5 * * * *'` and `.spec.concurrencyPolicy='Forbid'`.
questions.hint: `kubectl -n workloads-learn create cronjob report --image=busybox:1.36 --schedule='*/5 * * * *' -- sh -c 'date'` then edit (or patch) to set `concurrencyPolicy: Forbid`. Or write the YAML directly.
questions.solution:
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: report
  namespace: workloads-learn
spec:
  schedule: "*/5 * * * *"
  concurrencyPolicy: Forbid
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          restartPolicy: Never
          containers:
          - name: report
            image: busybox:1.36
            command: ["sh","-c","date"]
EOF
kubectl -n workloads-learn get cronjob report

verification.description: CronJob report has schedule '*/5 * * * *' and concurrencyPolicy Forbid
